events.title: Israel parliament elects Gadi Eisenkot ally Matan Kahana as new speaker
events.summary: Eisenkot’s bloc has pledged to undo some of Netanyahu’s most contentious policies following Kahana’s election. Israeli lawmakers have elected Matan Kahana as the new parliament speaker , marking a step towards reversing domestic policies from the outgoing government led by Benjamin Netanyahu. Kahana, an ally of Gadi Eisenkot – the party leader currently working to form the next government and replace Netanyahu – was voted in on Tuesday, receiving 66 votes in the 120-member chamber. list 1 of 3 Is Israel’s Eisenkot bloc less right wing than Netanyahu? list 2 of 3 Will Netanyahu lose this time? list 3 of 3 As Knesset readies for new speaker, Israeli opposition holds powerful role Netanyahu’s Likud party had put forward Ofir Katz as its own candidate. He received 52 votes following a stormy debate that stretched over seven hours. The Israel parliament speaker is an important office given that it sets the timetable for parliamentary business and can therefore speed up or delay debates or votes on proposed legislation. “I will be a Knesset speaker for everyone, irrespective of race, religion or gender,” said Kahana during his inauguration speech immediately after the vote. Kahana, a 54-year-old former special forces soldier, is expected as soon as Wednesday to start the process of undoing much of Netanyahu’s domestic agenda, especially regarding contentious reforms to the judiciary. Netanyahu is Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, having been in and out of office for three decades. The vote took place weeks after October 27 parliamentary elections in which neither Eisenkot nor Netanyahu won a majority in the Knesset, with the two blocs trading barbs since then. Eisenkot’s wide-ranging bloc secured 48 seats, while Netanyahu’s finished with 53. Two Arab-majority slates won an unprecedented 19 seats on the back of anger over Netanyahu’s hard-right government. On Tuesday, the two lists voted for Eisenkot’s candidate Kahana as parliament speaker, with one Arab Knesset member absent. Netanyahu’s and Eisenkot’s parties met on Sunday to discuss the possibility of joining a unity government but the meeting appeared to be largely a formality, with both men saying they should be prime minister. Netanyahu, who has reportedly been urging US President Donald Trump to resume the war on Iran, has talked up the threat from Tehran as he insists on the need for a unity government. With Kahana at the helm and if Eisenkot retains the backing of the Arab-Israeli parties, he has an opportunity to deal serious blows to Netanyahu’s legislative agenda even before a possible government is formed. Eisenkot has said he wants to rescind sweeping reforms to reduce the independence of the judiciary that were advanced by Netanyahu, who has been enraged over corruption charges against him that could land him in prison if he loses power. Eisenkot has also vowed to quickly set up a state commission of inquiry to investigate security failures that led to Hamas’s October 7, 2023 attack. Netanyahu, who has built his brand on saying he will ensure Israel’s security, has refused an independent probe, instead proposing one whose members would be chosen by politicians. Kahana, who is now a member of Eisenkot’s Yashar party, served in a short-lived non-Netanyahu government in 2021 and 2022 as minister for religious services, during which he clashed with ultra-Orthodox Jews by seeking to reduce the power of the Chief Rabbinate. Kahana himself is an observant Jew, part of Eisenkot’s efforts to form a broad coalition that ranges from secular liberals to religious conservatives. As parliament speaker, Kahana succeeds Amir Ohana, a Netanyahu ally who has held the position since 2022.

events.title: Exclusive: Donald Trump Jr. signals investors underestimated AI pushback
events.summary: Donald Trump Jr. signaled that investors underestimated the political pushback to the AI ecosystem in an interview at Axios' annual BFD summit in New York. The big picture: The 2026 midterms reflected deep distrust of the AI race, with voters approving dozens of moratoriums on data centers — which President Trump rallied around. Driving the news: Trump Jr. asserted that "a lot of" the pushback "is manufactured." But he added "that doesn't mean it's not real" in an interview with Axios Pro Rata author Dan Primack Tuesday. "I think some of the big founders of the biggest [AI] companies out there probably have not done themselves the best service as [a] marketing department," he said, adding that they're "probably not the best messengers when they basically say, 'AI is gonna rule the world, and you should be thrilled about it.'" Asked by Primack if investors, peers or the pair themselves underestimated the populist pushback to AI, Trump Jr. said, "I think we saw that very clearly." He likened AI to other "any great innovation," but said, "This is gonna be one of those things, but it is going to take some time for people to learn how to adapt that into their regular lives." State of play: Trump Jr. spoke with Primack alongside 1789 Capital co-founder Omeed Malik, whose venture Trump Jr. joined in 2024. The investment firm has since exploded from overseeing a few hundred million dollars to billions. Zoom in: Trump Jr. agreed that the rage toward data centers represents a broader concern over growing AI influence. That public anger is becoming key to candidates: Democrats in six early 2028 primary states expect their presidential nominee to prioritize AI regulations, according to new polling data first reported by Axios' Maria Curi. Ahead of the midterms, Republicans took note of the sagging views of the data centers needed to power the AI boom. While Trump has prioritized self-regulation for the industry, the November results raise questions about how Republicans will tackle the tech moving forward. Zoom out: Asked if there was anything Democrats and the White House could agree on after a November shellacking that could be good for business, he said "we've got to focus" on costs and inflation. But he argued that "the second they win ... it's about investigations" — which Trump Jr. could find himself targeted by. Editor's note: This story was updated with additional context throughout.

events.title: "We will remain thoughtful": Nvidia says it will continue to backstop AI ecosystem
events.summary: Nvidia's interim CEO said Tuesday that the company will be "disciplined" as it decides how much to invest in neoclouds and other AI customers going forward. Why it matters: Nvidia isn't just the biggest chip partner for AI startups — it's a major source of capital . What they're saying: "Our momentum is real," interim CEO Colette Kress said on at the end of conference call with investors and analysts. "Our demand is accelerating. Our supply is growing. Our customers and our partners are with us, and employees are committed. We've got this." She said the company would continue to use its balance sheet and support startups and the broader AI ecosystem, but she made clear it won't be a blank check. "As the market matures and additional sources of capital become available, we are rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments, and guarantees," she added. In particular, Kress said the company would continue to be "disciplined and selective in our support" for so-called neoclouds . Those companies provide additional computing capacity to big AI players as well as smaller and regional operators. "Our neoclouds have been so instrumental in terms of both supporting enterprises and supporting many of the different countries around the world." CoreWeave and Nebius, two such neoclouds, each ose by more than 10% in after-hours trading. Zoom in: Kress didn't name-check any other specific customers but said the company would offer capital to suppliers to help them move quickly. Nvidia will provide financing assistance or guarantees to some "very strong customers," she said. The chip-maker will "look very deeply" into whether guarantees are needed and conduct "a lot of work to understand if those are the right types of investments we need to make." Catch-up quick: Huang resigned last week after revelations that he had a relationship with a woman who allegedly had ties to Chinese intelligence. She was also a major Nvidia customer and helped Chinese AI companies gain access to cutting-edge Nvidia technology while the U.S. had banned some chip sales to the country. On the call, Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones through cold water on the notion of a quick return for Huang . "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," he said. The company said it wouldn't be taking questions on Huang's departure or its ongoing investigation into his actions.

events.title: California bans Waymo self-driving cars from freeways
events.summary: State DMV says vehicles pose ‘imminent hazard’ after cars entered closed zone and tried to bypass highway patrol California has banned Waymo’s autonomous vehicles from state freeways, saying they pose an “imminent hazard” after a spate of recent incidents. The restrictions, issued last Wednesday, bar Waymo from “operating or testing its driverless vehicles on all California freeways,” Jonathan Groveman, a spokesperson for the state’s department of motor vehicles, said in a statement. The measure comes after three of Waymo’s autonomous vehicles “entered an active construction closure” south of San Francisco on 5 November and another incident the next day involving highway patrol vehicles on a highway in San Francisco, according to the department. Video of the 6 November incident circulated widely on social media last week. In the footage, a Waymo vehicle can be seen trying to bypass California highway patrol vehicles conducting a traffic break. “The department determined that Waymo’s driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present,” Groveman said, adding that “similar incidents” previously occurred on 18 May. Waymo’s autonomous vehicles expanded on to freeways and interstates around San Francisco, Los Angeles and Phoenix last year. The Alphabet subsidiary operates the largest fleet of self-driving cars in the US. A Waymo spokesperson said in a statement that the “recent freeway construction zone encounters on US 101 in California” did not “involve any injuries or collisions” and that the company prioritized safety. “In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance,” the spokesperson said. “We are working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations.” A weekly dive in to how technology is shaping our lives Waymo continues to operate the vehicles as normal on California city streets, according to the company. California’s restrictions will remain in effect until “Waymo demonstrates to the department that it has taken effective corrective actions to address the deficiencies that precipitated the restrictions”, Groveman said.

events.title: Haitians protest in support of El Salvador’s anti-gang troop deployment
events.summary: El Salvador’s security minister has confirmed the troops will leave once kidnapped technicians are rescued. Demonstrators have marched in several Haitian cities to show support for a deployment of troops from El Salvador, despite concerns that the outside intervention may worsen instability in the Caribbean country. On Tuesday, hundreds of protesters rallied in the streets of cities like the capital, Port-au-Prince, bearing signs with slogans like “Down with the gangs”. list 1 of 3 Salvadoran troops target Haitian gang, leaving 20 dead list 2 of 3 Mauricio Pochettino announced as new Manchester United manager list 3 of 3 Widow of Haiti’s slain leader Moise to contest presidential vote Haiti has long struggled with gang violence, but the crisis worsened around 2021, after the assassination of President Jovenel Moise. His death further weakened Haiti’s central government, and experts say gangs took advantage of the eroding public confidence to expand their influence. The October 18 kidnapping of four Salvadoran aviation technicians near Port-au-Prince prompted El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele to respond with a military operation to Haiti. But on Monday, El Salvador confirmed it would end its deployment of about 2,500 troops once the missing Salvadoran airmen were found. “If they reappear tomorrow, as President Bukele said, we will leave,” Salvadoran Security Minister Gustavo Villatoro said. That announcement, however, was followed by public gestures of support and diplomatic engagements, with some top officials in Haiti encouraging the Salvadoran deployment to stay. Haitian Justice Minister Patrick Pelissier travelled to San Salvador on Monday and expressed gratitude for the troop surge. “The Haitian people applaud the decision of Nayib Bukele to send troops,” Pelissier said on Monday. He added that Haitian security forces, together with their international counterparts, had recently managed to regain control of Haiti’s national football stadium, held by gangs for years. “During the operation, we discovered several human skulls inside the stadium,” Bukele claimed in a social media post last week. The timeline for the Salvadoran troop withdrawal is uncertain. While El Salvador has framed its deployment as a rescue mission, the leader of Haiti’s 400 Mawozo gang, Wilson Joseph, told The Associated Press that the four technicians are already dead. Joseph added that the abduction took place in territory controlled by Chen Mechan, a rival gang. He provided no evidence to back his assertions. Bukele, however, has championed his country’s role in confronting Haiti’s gangs, using social media to promote the offensive and sharing videos of military operations. The Salvadoran president — who once referred to himself as the “world’s coolest dictator” — has been credited with popularising a “mano dura” or “strong hand” approach to regional security. Faced with one of the highest homicide rates in the world, Bukele launched a hardline security crackdown on gangs in El Salvador in 2022, including mass arrests and mass trials. His heavy-handed approach has led to a sharp decline in crime but has also been widely condemned for human rights abuses. Critics have warned that transplanting such tactics to Haiti could spark a backlash, leading to greater instability and risks to civilians. They have also criticised the lack of long-term planning for El Salvador’s troop deployment; a sudden withdrawal, for instance, could worsen the situation for Haiti’s security forces. Bukele is campaigning for a third term in El Salvador’s February presidential election, and analysts speculate his actions in Haiti could be used as a campaign tool to drum up support. The Salvadoran deployment is the latest in a series of international interventions in Haiti. Such foreign involvement is often controversial. The United States, for instance, has sent troops to Haiti on multiple occasions in the 20th century, occupying the country for decades and seizing control of its central bank. More recently, a United Nations-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF) arrived in Haiti in April, to help address the widespread gang violence. Gangs control more than 80 percent of the capital region. The conflict has killed more than 22,000 people since 2022. UN reports attribute more than half of the deaths in the first nine months of the year to security operations, including the deaths of 300 civilians. The UN also says almost 2,000 people have been displaced since the arrival of Salvadoran troops. But Pelissier said Haiti’s government had not reported any civilian casualties in the latest operations, which he described as professional. “The best to do is to avoid, as much as possible, human rights violations, and that’s what we are doing together,” the minister said.

events.title: Nvidia says its open source AI strategy remains intact after Jensen Huang’s exit
events.summary: Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress reaffirmed the company’s commitment to open source AI during Tuesday’s earnings call with analysts — the first since CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation. “At Nvidia, we are committed to fostering a vibrant open model ecosystem, so every country, company, and industry can build its own intelligence,” Kress said in her opening remarks. She also noted that open models were accelerating AI adoption, citing a 35-fold year-over-year surge in weekly token volume on OpenRouter, including a 3.5-fold increase over the past three months. Kress also spoke about Nvidia’s plans for Hugging Face, a platform for open source AI models that the company agreed to acquire for $12.9 billion in September, in what would be the second-largest acquisition in Nvidia’s history. The platform, which serves more than 118 million developers and 200,000 companies, is still on track to join Nvidia, despite Huang’s ouster. Huang had heavily advocated for open source AI technology. His departure had raised questions about the company’s future approach to open source AI models, with Hugging Face’s CEO calling Huang’s departure “a sad day,” and promising to “keep fighting for open-source AI, harder than ever.” So far, Nvidia’s plans for Hugging Face appear unchanged. The acquisition was not directly addressed during the Q&A portion of the earnings call. “Together, we will scale its platform and make intelligence more open, more capable, and more accessible,” said Kress of Nvidia’s plans for Hugging Face. Last week, Nvidia founder Huang resigned from his position as CEO following news about his extramarital affairs, including one with Alice Huang, an executive at the Singapore-based company Megaspeed who is suspected of being a Chinese spy. He’s also accused of having extramarital affairs with two direct reports and is now set to testify before Congress by Thanksgiving. Meanwhile, the SEC is investigating Nvidia over whether the company’s disclosures misled investors, The WSJ reported . Within Nvidia, Huang pushed for the development of the Nemotron family of open-weight AI models built for long-running agentic AI systems and reasoning workloads. On today’s call, Kress noted that Nemotron is now the “most widely used U.S. open model on OpenRouter,” and it’s “where developers start to build their own intelligence.” “That foundation is empowering the ecosystem,” she said. events.title: Yum China CEO Joey Wat: What China’s consumer market can teach global business
events.summary: In 1987, KFC opened its first restaurant in Beijing, marking the debut of China’s first Western quick-service restaurant brand. Nearly four decades later, KFC China has expanded to more than 14,000 stores in a market that has transformed around it. KFC has changed alongside it. In addition to the Original Recipe Chicken and Zinger, our menu offers energy bowls and sparkling coffee – many of which cannot be found in KFC menus outside China. More broadly, we have adapted everything from marketing to store formats as consumer preferences, technology and competition have evolved. For any global brand, keeping pace with such change requires tremendous effort. I believe one reason KFC has been able to keep adapting is the strength of our local teams. They have the know-how and autonomy to respond to the market with agility. The brand may be global, but decisions are made close to the consumer. KFC is one of the six restaurant brands operated by Yum China , which together span 20,000 stores across the country. Our experience, including 10 years as a company listed on the New York Stock Exchange, has reinforced three lessons for global brands seeking to win in this market. While shaped in China, I believe they extend far beyond it. First, a dual focus on innovation and efficiency is essential to survival and prosperity. One fundamental reality about China is that it is not a single market, but many. Consumer preferences, consumption occasions and competitive landscapes vary across regions and city tiers. A single playbook is not enough to win, which is why we tailor store formats and menus for select lower-tier cities. Yet highly tailored solutions can be costly, making a dual focus on innovation and efficiency essential. Yum China’s 20,000-store portfolio gives us a strong platform. Two years ago, we began carving out space within existing KFC stores for side-by-side modules such as KCOFFEE cafés to tap into fast-growing coffee demand. Since then, KCOFFEE cafes have expanded to over 4,000 locations, driving incremental sales and profit without incurring the investment of a new store. We have also extended this approach to KFC’s KPRO and Pizza Hut’s Burger Bar to capture the emerging light meal and the large burger market respectively. Consumers look for exciting new products and great value. We meet those needs by launching 500-600 new or upgraded products a year across our brands. To make this both efficient and sustainable, we draw inspiration from hero products to launch innovations such as the Intriguing Oreo Original Recipe Chicken Burger and Pizza Dough Burgers. As we drive transaction growth and tap into smaller-order occasions, we have been able to sustain the margins. Doing so requires transformation across nearly every part of the business, from supply chain and operations to technology. This is why innovation and efficiency can reinforce each other: innovative solutions drive efficiency, and efficiency in turn creates room for further innovations. Second, be patient enough to build what people cannot yet see. In fast-moving markets, there is constant pressure to focus on visible results. But resilience in challenging times requires investment in capabilities whose value may not be immediately apparent. I often think of bamboo, common across southern China, including my hometown in Fujian Province. Its strength lies underground, in roots that grow deep and wide, forming a complex, mutually reinforcing web. When green shoots finally emerge, they can grow with astonishing speed and become a forest that can weather storms. A business follows a similar pattern. The capabilities that make scale possible are often invisible for years. At Yum China, we have invested patiently in a root system: supply chain, digital and membership ecosystems, food innovation and organizational strength. These capabilities allow new concepts to draw on systems that have been built and strengthened over decades, rather than starting from scratch. Bamboo teaches us patience and discipline. Invest in the foundation, and trust that scale will follow. It also reminds us that success is interconnected. Like the roots of a forest, strong businesses reinforce one another. Third, people matter even more than strategy. When I was 15, I worked part-time as a restaurant food runner. It taught me the dignity of hard work and the importance of frontline employees. That experience shaped a belief I still hold today: employees come first, followed by customers and shareholders. This may sound like sacrilege to some, particularly for a public company, but it is essential to creating sustainable long-term value. Take care of employees, who shape customer experiences. Customers enable business performance. Business performance ultimately drives shareholder returns. Frontline employees often see changes in consumer sentiment and behavior early. They spot problems before they appear on dashboards. Having the right strategy is important, but without the right people to execute it, it cannot succeed. Put simply, execution is growth. This people-first mindset matters even more in the age of AI. AI can help forecast demand and optimize staffing. But these systems are only effective when they are built on the knowledge and judgment of experienced operators. As agentic AI begins to reshape how companies operate, one of the most undervalued assets in any organization may be its experienced operators – the “old masters” who understand the business deeply and can guide the integration of new technology into real workflows. Technology alone does not create advantage. People who know how to apply it do. The same lesson applies to global companies seeking to sustain success in China. Many strong local companies are founder-led. They move with speed, focus and entrepreneurial conviction. To compete effectively, multinational companies need local teams with good judgment and enough autonomy to respond just as quickly. China’s lesson for U.S. business leaders is clear: brand heritage can open doors and global scale can create powerful advantages. But both become liabilities if they breed complacency or slow decision-making. The real test is not whether a company can succeed in a market once. It is whether it can keep adapting as consumers and technology evolve. It is no longer enough for leaders to see where the future is headed. The best leaders build organizations capable of riding on the opportunities and challenges. events.title: New UK-EU youth mobility scheme may not fully launch until 2030
events.summary: Exclusive: deal expected to be sealed in principle at EU-UK summit on Friday but trickier elements could be postponed for six months The new post-Brexit UK-EU youth mobility scheme may not come fully into force until 2030. It will be a disappointment to any under-30s in the UK and the EU who hoped to travel, work or study in each other’s territories from next year after the long-awaited new deal. EU ambassadors will discuss the latest draft joint statement at a meeting on Wednesday in Brussels, with talk of youth mobility going right to the wire. “We aim to apply this agreement no later than 2028 and endeavour to ensure that opportunities under the scheme will be available to our young people no later than January 2030,” a draft text agreed by negotiators from London and Brussels says. The two sides aim to come to a “supplementary agreement” on tuition fees for EU citizens in UK universities. The text on this most contentious subject is not yet agreed with two alternatives mooted in the draft text – either a deal that students pay a reduced international fee or, alternatively, the same fee as UK nationals. The aim is that this would be agreed separately within six months. This is to allow linkage with the Made in Europe legislation that will not reach its final stages until possibly April next year in a vote in the European parliament. The legislation is designed to give priority to EU supply chains in the car and other industries. By linking the two issues the UK can get assurances that the final detail of the deal on mobility cannot be signed off unless it has been included in the Made in Europe legislation. EU countries including Germany could accept an unlimited number of young Britons under a youth mobility scheme, according to sources. Fresh details on how a scheme might work have emerged with EU leaders and the UK expected to settle on a quota of about 100,000 a year being allowed to work, travel or study in each other’s territories. The UK has insisted on a quota of EU citizens entering the UK under the scheme to guard against mass migration, but some countries have said they will not follow suit on the other side of the Channel and would be open to taking unlimited numbers. The quota is expected to be worked out on a country-by-country basis with smaller countries such as Malta and Luxembourg seeking a system that will not be based on a per-capita quota per EU member state. The new agrifood deal would not be agreed until 1 March 2028, the draft statement seen by the Guardian confirms. In what looks to be a breakthrough for Burnham there may also be a commitment to enter a dialogue to remove barriers to touring artists, particularly bands and theatres companies that perform in multiple EU member states. The 72-point joint statement also paves the way for further deals on steel between the UK and the EU. But there is no agreement yet on whether the UK would commit to dynamically aligning with the EU on trade defence measures such as tariffs on Chinese cars. The details came as Burnham said there is “no rush” to decide on the UK’s longer-term relationship with the EU, as he came under pressure from his own party to press the brakes on the pace of the rethink. The prime minister said he would “take stock” of the wider relationship after Friday’s summit in Brussels, at which he also hopes to secure agreements on food and farming and emissions trading. In an interview with Sky News, Burnham admitted he would now not set out the full options for a closer EU relationship until December – but denied he was “stepping back” from his previous commitments to pursue ties.

events.title: The US Navy used expired munitions against Iran in a workaround the top official compared to eating old bread
events.summary: The USS Delbert D. Black fires a Tomahawk missile during Operation Epic Fury. US Navy The Navy fired recoded, expired munitions during the Iran war, acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao said. Cao compared the practice to reviving stale bread with water and a microwave. The disclosure comes amid concerns about US missile stockpiles and production bottlenecks. The US Navy fired expired munitions during its war with Iran after changing their ammunition condition codes, the service's top civilian official told lawmakers Tuesday, comparing the practice to reviving stale bread with water and a microwave. Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao made the disclosure during his Senate confirmation hearing Tuesday, as lawmakers questioned the Pentagon's heavy expenditure of costly precision weapons during Operation Epic Fury . "A lot of the munitions we used in Epic Fury, we were able to recode those," Cao said. "They were Code Echo, Code Foxtrot, which means they're expired." According to a Defense Logistics Agency manual, codes Echo and Foxtrot represent materiel currently unserviceable but that could otherwise undergo limited restoration or repair. Cao, a retired Navy captain and former explosive ordnance disposal officer, compared the practice to stretching food supplies. "I came from a poor family," he said. "Things like bread, doesn't expire. You just rub some water on it and microwave for 15 seconds, and it's good to go." Cao did not identify which particular munitions were recoded or how many were fired. Many of the precision weapons the US used in the Iran war cost millions of dollars each, potentially making the ability to restore and use older stock useful in a pinch. The disclosure came while responding to Sen. Deb Fischer, a Nebraska Republican, who asked whether the Navy was striking the right balance between expensive precision weapons and cheaper weapons that could be produced in mass numbers. Cao said the Navy had increased Tomahawk cruise missile production from roughly 125 annually during his military career to more than 60 a month now. Cao's remarks come after months of worry surrounding whether the Pentagon has adequate quantities of costly missiles and other munitions on hand. A Pentagon Inspector General report released in September cited findings from the Office of the Under Secretary for Acquisition and Sustainment that the munitions expenditures throughout the war with Iran had resulted in "strategic inventory shortfalls and revealed industrial base bottlenecks for munitions resupply." events.title: Nvidia says it doesn’t plan to reappoint Jensen Huang as CEO
events.summary: Despite Nvidia founder and former CEO Jensen Huang’s recent offer to return to the chip company he helped build from the ground up, the company is not looking to take him back. During the company’s earnings call on Tuesday, Nvidia chairman Harvey C. Jones told listeners that Huang’s return was not something that company leadership was considering. “On November 12, our board of directors announced that after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company’s code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms,” Jones said, “Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as president, CEO, and board member. The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” On Tuesday, Huang had posted on X that since he left the company, he has “seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” and added that “if the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.” Huang resigned last week in dramatic fashion following revelations of a number of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman who has been accused of being a Chinese intelligence agent. That woman, former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, has maintained close ties to the former Nvidia CEO for years. Critics worry that the relationship may have influenced Nvidia’s dealings with China , and U.S. intelligence officials have expressed suspicions that she works for China’s Ministry of State Security. The development has sent shockwaves throughout the tech industry at a moment when the future of the AI business, in which Nvidia plays a pivotal role, hangs in the balance. It has also spurred investigations, including an independent investigation into Huang’s activities by Nvidia’s board and an SEC probe into Nvidia . Huang has been replaced by interim CEO Colette Kress , who is also the chipmaker’s chief financial officer and executive vice president, while the board searches for a permanent replacement. events.summary: Security All Security Cyber-crime Patches Research CSO Off-Prem All Off-Prem Edge and IoT Channel PaaS and IaaS SaaS On-Prem All On-Prem Systems Storage Networks HPC Personal Tech Cx0 Public Sector Software All Software AI and ML Applications Databases DevOps OS Platforms Virtualization Offbeat All Offbeat Columnists Supercomputing BOFH Legal Site News About Us Special Features All Special Features SC 26 Supercomputing Month 2026 Nvidia GTC Berlin 2026 Cybersecurity Month 2026 VMware Explore 2026 Cloud Infrastructure Month 2026 HPE: AI Explainers Agentic AI The Future of the Datacenter AWS:Reinvent Nvidia GTC Computex 2026 AI Infrastructure Month 2026 The State of Storage 2026 RSA Conference Vendor Voice All Vendor Voice Modernizing Financial Services with FIS and AWS Barco Infinidat Everpure Rubrik Make it real with Capgemini and AWS Money Movement Hub ZTE Nutanix: Scale Kubernetes. AWS New Horizon Digicert Netscout Resources Intelligence Webinars & Events Newsletters Nvidia unveils an HPC-optimized Rubin GPU to challenge AMD's 288 teraFLOPS MI430X Jensen Huang thrilled to be spending time with family, but will retake leadership burden if Nvidia asks 4 hours ago Python parallel debugging comes to HPC thanks to TotalView upgrade 5 hours ago America's hyperscale bit barns draw as much power as entire states 7 hours ago Hackers smash 'n' grab AI vendor: Take off with license data of Uber drivers 9 hours ago Nvidia places chip exports under boardroom supervision after Huang's exit 10 hours ago At Supercomputing 2026 this week, Nvidia unveiled a new variant of its Rubin GPUs aimed at – you’ll never believe it – high performance computing (HPC). The creatively named Rubin HPC promises more than 50,000 CUDA cores, nearly twice that of the AI-focused version of the chip that Nvidia unveiled earlier this year. It will arrive sometime in 2028. According to Dan Ernst, Nvidia’s senior director of supercomputing, the new chip offers a rebalanced architecture optimized for the kinds of simulation, engineering, and high-performance analytics workloads common in the HPC and scientific computing communities. This is not the first time Nvidia has introduced specialized hardware. Last year, the company optimized its B300 accelerator for AI inferencing workloads. “Rubin HPC is the same idea,” Ernst told El Reg . “Within the Rubin platform, but we’re building variants to really focus on a specific sub domain of applications.” Details remain remarkably thin. Nvidia hasn’t disclosed peak performance memory capacity or bandwidth. That said, the chip will likely include features which show Nvidia can think beyond AI and still cares about the HPC community. Fearing that Nvidia could ignore HPC is reasonable becuase beginning with the launch of Blackwell Ultra (B300/GB300), the company traded double-precision matrix acceleration for higher throughput at lower-precisions. The result was a chip that at FP4 churned out 15 petaFLOPS of AI compute, but just 1.3 teraFLOPS at FP64. That's good for AI, but less useful for scientists. When Nvidia unveiled Rubin, it seemed the GPU-slinger would continue this trend. At 33 teraFLOPS, the chip was not only slower at FP64 than the Blackwell GPUs it replaced, but slower than Nvidia’s now four-year-old Hopper accelerators as well. Nvidia contended that for sparse vector-heavy workloads measured by the High Performance Conjugate Gradients (HPCG) benchmark, the higher ratio of memory bandwidth to compute should deliver meaningful performance gains. Meanwhile, for dense matrix-heavy workloads, for which benchmarks like High-Performance Linpack (HPL) are representative, Nvidia adopted a new strategy: FP64 emulation. We discussed the pros and cons of this technique in greater detail earlier this year, but in a nutshell it uses an algorithm derived from the so-called Ozaki Scheme. The algorithm works by decomposing FP64 matrix operations into a string of INT8 operations that, when run on Nvidia’s tensor cores, achieve higher-than-native performance. Nvidia, we’re told, isn’t using INT8, but it is unlocking substantial performance gains, at least for certain workloads. According to Nvidia, Rubin can churn out up to 200 emulated FP64 matrix teraFLOPS. While Ernst didn’t offer any specifics, he assured us that Nvidia’s HPC hardware should offer native FP64 matrix performance and customers won't have to rely entirely on emulation. Assessing the new chip's vector performance is much easier. With more than 50 thousand CUDA cores (by our calculation, it should be closer to 53,248), the chip should deliver at least 86 percent higher vector performance at double precision. AMD is also cooking up new HPC chips. In a blog post published late last week, AMD revealed the HPC-tuned version of its MI400-series GPUs. The Instinct MI430X boasts 432 GB of HBM4, 23 TB/s of memory bandwidth and a whopping 288 teraFLOPS of peak double precision grunt. AMD isn’t relying on FP64 emulation.

events.title: Trump ‘reaches out a lot’: Jeff Bezos says shutting out business leaders is a mistake
events.summary: Amazon founder Jeff Bezos says he doesn’t regret aligning himself with President Donald Trump, calling him unusually “communicative.” “He reaches out a lot,” Bezos said at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World, adding that it was “quantitatively unusual.” It’s a two way street — with the billionaire and the president both calling one another, he added. The billionaire said he’s worked closely with every president since Bill Clinton and plans to work with “every president going forward as long as they’ll have me,” sidestepping a question on whether tying himself so closely to the administration might create difficulties in a Democrat-controlled Congress. “I’m on the side of America,” he said. “I have never tried to take advantage for Amazon or myself or any of my companies. So, you know, presidents need advice from business leaders, and shutting out business leaders is a mistake. It’s not smart.” Former President Barack Obama was very communicative too, Bezos said. “I still reach out to Obama for advice” but none of the other presidents “were half as communicative as Trump is” when it comes to the sheer volume of conversations, Bezos said. Blue Origin taps Prometheus Bezos said he’s spending most of his time these days focusing on Prometheus, his artificial intelligence startup that aims to bring AI to the physical world. He said his space company Blue Origin is already utilizing Prometheus tools on two projects, declining to provide details of how the space business is putting the startup’s products to work. When asked whether he’d follow rival Elon Musk, who’s trying to merge all of his businesses together, Bezos said he didn’t have plans to stitch Prometheus, Blue Origin, and Amazon together. “That’s such a funny idea,” he said. “I have nothing to announce.” Prometheus was founded in 2025 and has so far raised $14.5 billion and employs around 250 people, Bezos said. Vik Bajaj, co-founder of Prometheus, said that they respect the “proprietary nature” of engineering when working with other companies, but can help to shorten their product development significantly. “We help them perform their work much, much, much faster than is possible without the tools that we’re developing,” Bajaj said. Nvidia Bezos also had some advice for the Nvidia board: don’t hire from outside the company. He urged the board to look internally for a replacement, if they don’t bring former CEO Jensen Huang back on, that is. Bezos did skirt around the question of whether or not Huang should be reinstated, saying he didn’t “know enough of the details.” “There’s probably a bunch of stuff that happened inside those board meetings and so on that we don’t know,” he said. He said that an outside pick would have a “vanishingly small chance of success” given Nvidia’s complex business. An outside candidate for CEO should be treated as a “last resort.” Bond It was immediately clear to everyone in the room, including director Denis Villeneuve, that Robert Pattinson should be the next James Bond, Jeff Bezos said at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World. Although they weren’t always sold on the actor due to his level of fame, the choice became clear through “old fashioned” screen testing. “He is James Bond,” Bezos said. The search had previously been whittled down to just five names, but ultimately the choice was “undebated.” — Ellen DiMauro

events.title: Hundreds of websites deliver potent malware cocktail to unsuspecting visitors
events.summary: Hundreds of websites using the Optimizely website personalization platform served unsuspecting visitors a potent malware cocktail that targeted cryptocurrency wallets, stole payment card data, cookies, and screenshots, and delivered exploit kits for infecting iPhones and iPads, researchers said Tuesday. ReportURI said it identified 178 websites—including CNN, Zoom, the BBC, and Salesforce—that were affected. JavaScript digitally signed by Optimizely and then loaded into customer pages had been modified to include malicious components that attempted to infect visitor devices with multiple payloads. When wares were installed successfully, they swapped user cryptocurrency wallet addresses for the attackers. Other components skimmed payment cards, stole cookies and screenshots, and, on iPhones and iPads, delivered iOS exploit kits known as Coruna and DarkSword. Optimizely infrastructure delivers multipurpose malware Optimizely serves JavaScript “snippets” that include both company code and code that is provided by each customer. The JavaScript, which can be served directly from Optimizely or from a customer endpoint, runs on every page the customer serves. Somehow, the attackers wrote their own code into a portion of each affected customer’s JavaScript and then delivered it from cdn.optimizely.com. A valid certificate for that domain signed the JavaScript. Read full article Comments

events.title: Amazon and Google will together own nearly 30% of Anthropic after its IPO
events.summary: Anthropic on Tuesday disclosed more details about the biggest investment agreements with major cloud providers Amazon and Google. While we already knew that Amazon stood to make a killing on its Anthropic investments from the IPO, Anthropic revealed that Amazon’s total stake will come in at just shy of 15% (14.7% to be exact). Even more interesting is that Amazon could have, if it wished, owned an even bigger share of the company. When Amazon invested billions in Anthropic in 2023 and 2024 (long before Claude Code took the enterprise world by storm, back in the days when Anthropic looked like it would forever be a speck in OpenAI’s shadow), the cloud giant obtained promissory notes that could convert into equity. These notes carry conversion prices of about $2.09 or $5.05 per share, depending on the year of investment. Amazon has opted to convert a chunk of them as part of the IPO into a special class of non-voting shares that will give it about 15% ownership. (The shares can receive dividends and convert to standard voting Class A shares when sold, the filing says). But it has also opted to hold on to billions of dollars’ worth of the notes for now. If it converted them all right now, it would own just under 24% of Anthropic (23.8% to be precise). Google, meanwhile, will own just under 14% (13.7%), also in non-voting shares, which come from the conversion of notes, as well as the “private placement” sale of shares as part of this IPO. A group of major tech companies (AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia, and TSMC Partners) have agreed to buy $26 billion worth of this non-voting stock. Google and Nvidia each agreed to buy $10 billion worth. So while a lot of investors stand to make billions of dollars in Anthropic’s IPO, Amazon is one of the biggest winners, and that doesn’t even count that AWS stands to earn from Anthropic’s commitment to spend more than $100 billion on its cloud services over the next decade. events.title: Nvidia delivers strong results as investors weigh post-Huang future​
events.summary: Nvidia beat forecasts, with third-quarter revenue of US$115.84 billion and fourth-quarter guidance of US$130 billion, plus or minus 3%, above Wall Street estimates. Investors are worried after Jensen Huang resigned. Colette Kress is interim CEO, and the board is searching for a new leader while facing pressure over “Stand With Jensen”. The board set up a national security and export controls committee as US scrutiny grows. Nvidia also faces tighter chip rules for China, South-east Asia and overseas data centres. SAN FRANCISCO - Nvidia forecast quarterly revenue above Wall Street estimates on Nov 17, giving investors some relief after longtime leader Jensen Huang’s resignation plunged the chip firm into crisis. “Our momentum is real,” interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress said, without addressing the leadership uncertainty. “Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start, our roadmap is on track.” With Huang gone, investors are looking for clues about Nvidia’s future, from billions of dollars invested in cloud providers, suppliers and AI startups to who will ultimately lead the world’s most valuable chipmaker. The AI boom’s most prolific salesman resigned last week after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang and two Nvidia employees. US intelligence agencies are trying to determine the extent of Alice Huang’s ties to China’s Ministry of State Security and what information she may have passed to Beijing, according to two people familiar with the matter. Huang’s exit ended three decades of founder-led control over Nvidia’s chip roadmap, customer deals and Washington ties, making execution a bigger risk than near-term AI demand, analysts say. The company expects fourth-quarter revenue of US$130 billion, plus or minus 3%, above analysts’ average estimate of US$125.25 billion, according to LSEG data. Nvidia said the outlook assumes no data-center chip sales to China. Adjusted gross margin is expected at 71% to 72%, compared with analysts’ estimate of 71.7%. Finance chief Colette Kress is interim CEO, while the board considers internal and external candidates. A growing “Stand With Jensen” campaign has complicated the search, although the board is not considering Huang’s return, three people told Reuters on Nov 16. Huang said on Nov 17 he would be “honoured” to return if the board deemed it best. Earlier on Nov 17, Nvidia’s board created a committee on national security and export controls, its first major governance move since Huang’s departure, as scrutiny grows over the chipmaker’s national security role. Washington has also tightened licensing rules for chip shipments to South-east Asia and overseas data centers serving Chinese firms, while lawmakers prepare to question Huang, who had pushed for greater chip exports to China. Investors were already uneasy about AI spending after Democrats’ midterm sweep fueled fears of tougher scrutiny and slower data-center expansion. They also want to know whether Nvidia’s next CEO will continue financing customers, a practice critics call circular. The Nov 17 results offer a first read on Vera Rubin, Nvidia’s newest generation of AI processors and successor to Grace Blackwell. Nvidia said in August that Vera Rubin would account for about a fifth of data-center revenue in the October quarter and forecast 70% revenue growth in the next fiscal year. Nvidia’s third-quarter revenue more than doubled to US$115.84 billion, beating analysts’ estimate of $109.11 billion. The company has topped Wall Street’s revenue expectations for 17 straight quarters. Adjusted gross margin rose to 74.9% from 73.5% a year earlier, also beating analysts’ estimate of 74.1%, despite soaring memory prices and production ramps. REUTERS

A military plane has crashed in western Siberia, killing all 19 people on board, according to a statement from the Russian Defence Ministry, cited by local media. The Antonov An-12 transport aircraft went down in an unpopulated area near the city of Kemerovo, about 3,000km east of Moscow. The An-12 is a Soviet-built four-engine turboprop transport plane that has been in service since the late 1950s. events.title: Nvidia’s Board Has No Plans to Bring Back Jensen Huang
events.summary: As Nvidia reported its third-quarter earnings on Tuesday, the company’s financial performance was overshadowed by the drama surrounding its former CEO . And Nvidia’s board made one thing clear right off the bat: Jensen Huang isn’t coming back . At the start of the earnings call, Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones emphasized the company’s strength and “groundbreaking technology” before turning to the circumstances surrounding Huang’s departure. “On November 12, our board of directors announced that, after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company’s code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms, Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions … and the board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” Jones said. Asked about the company’s strategy for retaining talent and navigating the leadership transition, interim CEO Colette Kress emphasized the importance of the company’s workforce. “Our employees are absolutely instrumental to everything in this company,” Kress said. “We will take care of our employees during this transition to make sure that they are safe and that the work can be done in the current environment.” Jones added that the Nvidia board is taking the search for a new CEO “very seriously” and is considering both internal and external candidates. National security dynamics are changing the chip industry, Jones said, and “our new CEO will have to navigate those waters very carefully. So the search will be thorough. We want to install the permanent CEO as quickly as possible, but we won’t expedite the CEO before finding exactly the right person.” One recurring theme that emerged from the earnings call, aside from the Huang saga: Demand for Nvidia’s chips remains as strong as ever. Kress said that Nvidia expects that it will keep growing throughout 2027 and into 2028, fueled by the rise of agentic AI. Less than a week after Huang resigned as chief executive, Nvidia reported $115.8 billion in revenue for the quarter that ended on October 25, 2026. That exceeded analysts’ expectations of roughly $109 billion and was nearly double the revenue reported in the same quarter a year ago. The vast majority of Nvidia’s revenue came from its data center business, which generated $107.6 billion, up 110 percent from a year ago. Earlier this month, The New York Times reported that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset, who had served as an executive at a Singapore-based cloud provider called Megaspeed. Then, reports emerged that Nvidia’s longtime leader additionally had an affair with one of his direct reports; following Huang’s resignation, Reuters reported he had an affair with a second employee. Huang’s relationship with the alleged Chinese operative has raised questions about what he knew about Nvidia’s advanced chips making their way into China despite US export restrictions. Nvidia had placed Megaspeed on its “no sell” list in June 2025, but The New York Times reported that, according to third-party data, a subsidiary of Megaspeed “received shipments of more than $800 million of export-controlled Nvidia A.I. technology, including Blackwell and H200 chips,” which were subject to export restrictions. On the heels of Tuesday’s earnings, Nvidia’s stock rose in after-hours trading. The company had lost more than $1 trillion in market value over the past month amid the fallout from Huang’s scandal. Earlier on Tuesday, Huang released his first statement since his resignation. Huang thanked allies for their support, writing he’d “seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO.” He admitted to failing to “live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA,” adding he was “committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation.” However, Huang concluded, if the board “decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.” Nvidia, which is headquartered in Santa Clara, California, has roughly 60,000 employees, and sentiments have varied in the wake of Huang’s departure. “In just three days we went from superhero cape to ‘Oops, I forgot my pants,’ and nobody’s quite sure how to swallow that,” an employee told WIRED last week. But in his 33 years leading Nvidia, Huang earned a loyal army of supporters by minimizing layoffs and red tape. Some employees have been calling for his return to the helm. And a few tech industry heavyweights are similarly eager for Huang to be reinstated. Executives including Elon Musk , Replit CEO Amjad Masad , and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan took to X to voice support for Huang, signing a petition to “Bring Jensen Back.

events.title: NVIDIA Expands Commitments With Supply Chain Partners to Support AI Infrastructure Buildout
events.summary: News Summary: New agreements with Kinsus and Samsung Electro-Mechanics support additional substrate capacity and expanded production capabilities at existing factories. NVIDIA’s work with Amkor and SPIL expands advanced packaging capacity for current and next-generation accelerated computing platforms. NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 and Vera CPUs began volume shipments in the third quarter, leveraging TSMC’s 5nm, 3nm and CoWoS advanced packaging technologies. Foxconn is deepening its collaboration with NVIDIA, drawing on its global production network to support next-generation GPU and networking platforms. NVIDIA today announced expanded commitments with supply chain partners to support sustainable long-term growth, aligning supply and manufacturing capacity with demand for its accelerated computing and AI infrastructure platforms. Working with Amkor Technology, Foxconn, Kinsus Interconnect Technology, Samsung Electro-Mechanics , Siliconware Precision Industries (SPIL) and TSMC, NVIDIA is expanding manufacturing capacity across substrates, advanced packaging, wafer and contract manufacturing to scale production of its current and next-generation accelerated computing platforms. “Our supply chain is a strategic advantage,” said Debora Shoquist, executive vice president of operations at NVIDIA. “Our work with these partners builds on our manufacturing foundation for long-term growth, expanding capacity across components, advanced packaging and system production to deliver the accelerated computing platforms our customers need.” Increasing Substrate Capacity and Production Capabilities NVIDIA is expanding its substrate supply commitments with Kinsus and Samsung Electro-Mechanics, adding manufacturing capacity and improving production capabilities at existing factories. Under a new agreement with NVIDIA, Kinsus plans to expand its advanced ABF package substrate manufacturing capacity dedicated to NVIDIA by more than 3.5x over current levels from its Youth campus in Taoyuan, Taiwan. Production is expected to begin in the second half of 2027, with the additional capacity targeted for the third quarter of 2028. This multiyear agreement builds on the companies’ existing supplier relationship and supports NVIDIA’s long-term supply planning for its accelerated computing platforms. “We believe AI will be one of the most important technology transitions of our lifetime,” said Scott Chen, CEO and president of Kinsus. “After more than a decade of partnership with NVIDIA, we are excited to continue building the future together.” NVIDIA and Samsung Electro-Mechanics have amended their existing substrate supply agreement to improve operational capabilities at existing factories in support of increased production of NVIDIA’s accelerated computing platforms. events.title: Nike lays out financial goals ahead of first investor day in 9 years
events.summary: Nike is hosting its first investor day in nine years at its Oregon headquarters as the company tries to prove to investors that its turnaround strategy is working. The footwear company has been enduring a yearslong slump, including significant sustained declines in the China market. Nike said Tuesday ahead of its first investor day in nine years that it was reaffirming its 2027 financial guidance. The retailer also laid out a financial framework and said that by the end of fiscal 2031 it's targeting approximately $5 billion in incremental revenue growth from fiscal year 2027, operating margins of 12% to 14% and adjusted earnings per share of $3.00 to $3.50. The company said higher-quality revenue, gross margin expansion and productivity improvements would help it reach its goals. Nike's 2027 financial guidance includes expectations for revenue to decline in the high-single-digit range, an adjusted operating margin of approximately 6%, and adjusted EPS of $1.15 to $1.35. The company also introduced a strategy it's calling Full Stride Ahead, which the company said aims "to get closer to athletes and focus resources on the greatest opportunities for long-term growth." Nike CEO Elliott Hill told CNBC's Sara Eisen that the new initiative is about "being closer to the athletes we serve." "What's different today is the depth and breadth we're taking from an innovation perspective," Hill said. He added that Nike is emphasizing sportswear at a time when sports have never been more relevant around the world. Hill also said Nike is working to regain its cultural relevance, after a perceived dropoff contributed to its slowdown both in its home market and in China. Nike said it would focus on performance sports and sportswear opportunities "with the greatest potential for long-term growth," and said its five priority sports would be running, training, global football, basketball and outdoor. Nike is holding an investor day at its Oregon headquarters Tuesday as the company aims to prove to investors that its turnaround strategy is yielding success after a yearslong slump. Last month, the company reported mixed fiscal first-quarter results as it announced a restructuring plan, including layoffs that it said would start next year. It's the company's third round of layoffs to be announced this year. Nike's net income and revenue both fell during the most recent period compared with a year ago, and the company said it expects revenue to decline by a high single-digit percentage in fiscal 2027. The new strategy, dubbed Pace, focuses on the company's supply chain and reorganizing into three geographies. Nike said the turnaround plan is expected to deliver roughly $2.5 billion in savings through fiscal 2031. Nike has been seeing significant sustained declines in its China market, where revenue last quarter dropped 26%. Experts have said the company is losing relevance in the country, while Nike has said it's actively working to win over younger consumers. At the same time, Nike announced last quarter that it's creating a new global campus in India as part of its new growth strategy, hoping the country will help boost its performance. The company said it was remaining focused on China even as it begins to build out its India presence. Nike COO Venkatesh Alagirisamy told CNBC the company sees an opportunity to triple its business in the country over the next five years. He added that Nike's broader strategy will position it for success in India. "If you look at the three components, brand building, landing those innovations into marketplaces in an increasingly locally connected fashion and then doing all of those things in a much faster pace really aligns well with the aspirations for India," he said. CEO Elliott Hill's turnaround strategy includes improving different parts of the business at different rates based on priority. While it's seen some signs of progress in the North America business, Hill has said that performance isn't enough to offset the pressures on the company elsewhere, including internationally. The Nike consumer has also been under increased macroeconomic pressure as geopolitical tensions mount and inflation rises.

events.title: Nvidia posts strong earnings amid Jensen Huang exit, reported SEC probe
events.summary: Nvidia posted a stronger-than-expected third quarter and a bullish outlook in its first earnings report after Jensen Huang was ousted as CEO in a scandal that has reportedly spawned an SEC investigation. Why it matters: Nvidia remains squarely at the center of the AI economy — and investors are anxious for guidance on the company's strategic roadmap following Huang's sudden exit. Zoom in: Nvidia recorded quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion and net income of $65.3 billion, both more than doubling its performance from a year earlier. S&P Capital IQ analysts had expected revenue of $108.7 billion and net income of $60.5 billion. The company's data center revenue — its largest segment — rose 110% from a year ago to $107.6 billion. The showing — which included a whopping gross profit margin of 74.8% — immediately calmed investors who have shaved more than $1 trillion off of Nvidia's market cap since the Huang scandal broke. The stock was up 2% in after-hours trading Tuesday. It marks the first moment for interim CEO Colette Kress — who is also still serving as CFO — to exert her leadership during the most tumultuous moment in the company's history. She didn't mention Huang on Tuesday in the earnings report but touted Nvidia's role as "an exceptional technology leader" and said sales of the company's new, advanced Vera Rubin chips are "off to an explosive start." "Our roadmap is on track and our ambition has never been greater," she said. What we're watching: Whether Nvidia discloses any additional details about its CEO search or other investigations on its earnings call. WSJ reported Tuesday afternoon that the SEC has opened a civil probe into the company. An SEC spokesperson declined to comment. Nvidia reps did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Huang posted a public letter Tuesday saying he'd be "honored" to return as CEO. Newly appointed Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones said on Tuesday afternoon's earnings call that the board unanimously accepted Huang's resignation "and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO." Tech analyst Dan Ives earlier said the board could face a special shareholder meeting called by at least 15% of shareholders. What's next: Tech analyst Gene Munster said on X that the Nvidia earnings call Tuesday is "the most anticipated conference call of all time, and the one we'll likely get the least information from." Editor's note: This story was updated to include comments from Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones made on the company's earnings call.

events.title: ‘Wolf of Wall Street’ Jordan Belfort on his AI salespeople who are better than humans: ‘What if you have a bad apple that says stuff?’
events.summary: Just months after Jordan Belfort’s court-ordered restitution obligation ended, leaving his victims far short of the $110 million he was ordered to pay them, “The Wolf of Wall Street” is selling over the phone again, this time with AI bots trained on his sales techniques. Belfort’s new AI sales-voice startup, Tone, has brought in about $1 million in revenue so far, and he’s aiming for between $20 million and $30 million in recurring revenue within the next year. Belfort said Tone’s technology is more reliable than humans because companies can keep a firm grip on what it says. This contrasts with salespeople who can stray from approved scripts and could potentially cross a line with customers. “What if you have a bad apple that says stuff—maybe inadvertently even, right?” he said. Tone launched publicly on Nov. 16 with about $10 million raised, and Belfort said its API and a content creation platform goes live in about a week. It arrives as big companies move to automate customer calls— Verizon CEO Dan Schulman told Fortune this month the telecom giant is preparing to automate much of its routine customer service work—and two years after the FCC put AI-generated voices under federal robocall rules. A study by international cloud voice software company AVOXI found in September that just over half of organizations are already using AI voice agents, and a majority are planning to adopt them over the next two years. Tone’s offerings include 16 different male and female artificial voices ranging from higher to lower-pitched that are trained on Belfort’s tonal sales techniques. Unlike other AI voices, he said they adjust their intonation and volume, among other factors, to try to better influence listeners. This includes phrasing declarative statements as questions to show the listener you’re engaged, or speaking in a low voice to convey scarcity and the importance of the information, Belfort told Fortune . Those subtle vocal techniques, he argued, can make the difference between someone listening to a sales pitch or hanging up and will help the company compete against an increasingly crowded field of voice AI startups. The tech is not meant to replace salespeople but merely to expand the number of contacts they can reach, he added. Of the $10 million the company has raised ( TechCrunch first reported the figure), 70% of it came from friends and family and the rest from investors, he estimated. Better than humans? Yet Belfort also noted that Tone still has limitations, especially when it comes to navigating complicated conversations. To make conversations sound natural, Tone’s models have to respond within about 500 to 600 milliseconds. But that leaves only about 100 milliseconds for the AI to process a question and formulate an answer, which means the company is limited in the complexity of the models it can use to get the fastest response. As AI models improve and computer chips become faster, however, Belfort believes that trade-off will become less significant. “I would think in the next six months, at the most a year, that gap will be eliminated,” he said. A question of trust Belfort pleaded guilty and was later sentenced in 2003 for fraud and money laundering, spending 22 months in prison before being released in 2006. Since then, he has focused on motivational speaking and consulting. His memoir, “The Wolf of Wall Street,” also inspired the 2013 film by the same name starring Leonardo DiCaprio. Belfort was ordered by a federal judge in 2003 to pay $110 million in restitution, yet his court-ordered restitution obligation ended earlier this year, with TMZ reporting that his victims ultimately received a much lower amount than expected. As of 2018, Belfort had paid about $13 million of the total sum, according to court documents . The prospect of AI sales bots trained on the techniques of someone convicted of fraud raises ethical questions. Belfort’s cofounder, the venture capitalist Shervin Pishevar, has also faced sexual misconduct allegations , which he denies. There are also regulatory concerns. The Federal Communications Commission ruled in 2024 that AI-generated voices fall under existing restrictions on robocalls under the Telephone Consumer Protection Act, a federal law aimed at protecting consumers from unwanted telemarketing calls. The rules include exemptions for some noncommercial polling and survey calls to residential landlines. Belfort previously told TechCrunch that Tone makes outbound sales calls only to opted-in leads or existing customers. The company always recommends disclosing when customers are speaking to AI, he told Fortune . “I think it’s important that it should be disclosed, and I think the worst thing you’d want to break trust with someone—if they do at some point realize it, that would be, I think, a really bad thing,” he said. For now, Tone offers two languages, English and Spanish, but Belfort said it plans to add two to four more languages each month. In the future, he said Tone will develop AI-powered avatars to add virutal body language and facial expressions to its portfolio of persuasion tools during video calls. Despite his prior conviction, Belfort said he has spent the last two decades working to rebuild his reputation and is now working 14 hour days to build Tone. “I think that the company and the technology should speak for itself, and I think people need to make their own decision,” he said. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

events.title: Widespread outages hit banks, air travel, the NSA and Apple, disrupting seemingly everything
events.summary: Over four days, outages disrupted Microsoft services, the FAA, JPMorgan Chase transactions and Apple. Security researchers say AI is accelerating vulnerability discovery, increasing pressure on organizations to patch systems quickly. "When Microsoft goes down, the whole world comes to a standstill," said Raj Rajamani, CEO of JetStream Security. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton dismissed suspicions that malicious activity led to a series of outages at major tech firms and government agencies over the past week. "This is not cyberattack, and this is not a coordinated effort by a nation state," he told CNBC's "Closing Bell" on Tuesday. "We've looked very closely." It's been a tough few days for the technology world after a series of widespread disruptions brought different parts of life to a halt. On Tuesday, an outage halted internal communications at the National Security Agency, and iPhone maker Apple confirmed that different products were either down or having issues . The NSA pointed to "scheduled routine maintenance," while Apple cited "an internal update" as the reason behind its issues. It marked four major system problems in four consecutive business days. Microsoft 's Outlook issues wreaked havoc on businesses on Thursday, and the Federal Aviation Administration grounded flights on Friday. On Monday, issues at JPMorgan Chase affected customer transactions, and an outage at United Airlines briefly delayed departing flights. "When Microsoft goes down, the whole world comes to a standstill," said Raj Rajamani, CEO of JetStream Security. "That's a stark reminder of how deeply embedded these services and technologies are in our day-to-day life." The disruptions have rattled consumers and led to a steady stream of memes on social media, as people look for a silver lining — or sinister plot — in the string of technology problems. Experts say the real culprit behind this strange series of coincidences is much more benign. "We're in the weird teenage phase of technology not quite maturing enough to know how to do this without disrupting services and so forth," said Tom Hegel, research head at SentinelOne. Anthropic likely to price IPO above the current range of $70 to $78, sources tell CNBC Demis Hassabis’ AI company raises $5 billion, months after he left as Google DeepMind CEO OpenAI inks agreements with four independent evaluators to boost company’s safety work How Rockstar’s ‘GTA VI’ release could reshape gaming, streaming and even paid time off With the help of artificial intelligence, businesses are patching more software vulnerabilities than ever before and updating archaic systems to prepare for swarms of attacks in the wake of high-profile incidents like Hugging Face. That's leaving information technology and security teams strained and scrambling to keep up with heightened demand, said Sam Rubin, senior vice president of consulting and threat intelligence at Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42. Amid this prolonged period of uncertainty, Rubin said businesses should prioritize updating their most exploitable systems and keeping operations underway when an outage hits. "You need to think about how you continue to operate in the face of one of your IT systems going down," he said. Clayton told CNBC that routine upgrades are commonplace at any organization and called for a nationwide digital infrastructure upgrade. Last week, millions of users lost access to email in a fiasco that Microsoft eventually said was the result of an undetected bug that was lurking since July. The FAA, which is still looking into the root cause of its system failure, pointed in part to a router upgrade in southern Arkansas overseen by government contractor L3Harris Technologies that overwhelmed the agency's telecommunications network. JPMorgan said longer-than-usual service times on Monday stemmed from a software bug in on-premise hardware systems. Agencies and businesses have ruled out cyberattacks, but the routine patching alibi hasn't satisfied some skeptics, and lawmakers are calling for more transparency. Sen. Mark Warner, D-Va., on Tuesday used the recent incidents to make the case for an AI safety bill. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., acknowledged that it's "too premature" to conclude malicious activity but called for a congressional briefing. "I think it's time for the administration to come up to the Hill and explain themselves so we can be informed about the steps that need to be taken and we can inform the people of the United States of America," he said during a press conference on Tuesday.
